sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: NOT MEASURED — the ledger clips describe reporter knock-in mice used to identify Cntnap4-expressing cells; no surface-trafficking assay or functional assay for the tagged protein is reported in the cited clips.
sites.rationale: CNTNAP4 is a type-I single-pass transmembrane protein with its N-terminus extracellular (residues 26–1241) and its C-terminus intracellular (residues 1263–1308); the only extracellular terminus is the mature N-terminus beginning at Gly26. L2 explicitly states that the signal sequence (residues 1–25) was replaced by eGFP, placing the tag at the mature N-terminus; L3 corroborates with a second independent knock-in at the same locus. The topology-derived junction is insert_after_residue = 25 (Ala25 → Gly26), which is the signal-peptide cleavage site; a tag placed here is on the extracellular face and satisfies the ≥3-residue distance from the TM boundary (>1200 residues away). Because no residue number is explicitly named in either clip, position_evidence is topology_derived. Two independent knock-in mouse lines place eGFP at the N-terminus of full-length CNTNAP4/Caspr4. L2 (PMC4281262) describes a targeting vector that replaced the first exon (encoding the ATG and signal sequence, residues 1–25) with in-frame eGFP, yielding a full-length GFP-tagged protein. L3 (PMC3898991) describes a parallel Caspr4 GFP knock-in where GFP-pA is inserted immediately after the methionine start codon of the Caspr4 gene. No specific junction residue is named in either clip; the position is derived from the single extracellular terminus of this type-I transmembrane protein.

sources.claim: The Cntnap4 targeting vector was designed to replace a genomic fragment of 585 bp containing the first exon of the gene, encoding the ATG and the signal sequence, with an in frame egfp , followed by an oppositely directed neo gene ( Fig.1B ).

literature_notes: L1 and L2 are from the same paper (PMC4281262) and describe the same knock-in construct; L2 is cited as the primary clip because it is more explicit about the construct design (signal sequence replaced by eGFP). L3 (PMC3898991) independently corroborates the N-terminal eGFP placement in a separate Caspr4 knock-in line. All three ledger lines describe reporter knock-in mice; none explicitly confirms cell-surface display of the tagged protein, so validation_level is not_measured. The intracellular C-terminus (residues 1263–1308) is not a surface-tag site and is not proposed. No internal extracellular loop insertion is supported by any ledger line.
